subject: Biology
title: Chromosomal Mutations
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Chromosomal Mutations.

hook.text: Sometimes mutations are massive—whole chunks of chromosomes get deleted, duplicated, or flipped.

buildup.text: Deletion removes a segment. Duplication copies one. Inversion flips a section backward.

discovery.text: Translocation moves a piece from one chromosome to another, sometimes fusing genes.

twist.text: Down syndrome results from an extra copy of chromosome 21—three copies instead of two.

climax.text: Large mutations can disable many genes at once, but some fuel rapid evolutionary leaps.

punchline.text: Big mistakes sometimes lead to big changes.

quiz.question: What causes Down syndrome?
options: A point mutation in one gene

details.summary: Chromosomal mutations are large-scale changes to chromosome structure or number, including deletions, duplications, inversions, and translocations. Changes in chromosome number, like trisomy 21 causing Down syndrome, affect development when entire gene sets are altered.
details.whyItMatters: Chromosomal mutations cause major genetic disorders and also drive evolution by reshuffling large blocks of genetic material. Prenatal screening for chromosomal abnormalities is now routine in many countries.
takeaways: Deletions remove chromosome segments containing multiple genes
Trisomy adds an extra copy of an entire chromosome to every cell
Chromosomal rearrangements can create new gene combinations driving evolution

faq.question: What causes chromosomal mutations?
faq.answer: Most arise from errors during cell division when chromosomes fail to separate properly (nondisjunction) or break and rejoin incorrectly. Radiation, chemicals, and aging eggs increase the risk. Most are spontaneous rather than inherited.

faq.question: Why is trisomy 21 survivable while most trisomies are not?
faq.answer: Chromosome 21 is the smallest human autosome with relatively few genes. The extra copy disrupts development less severely than trisomy of larger chromosomes. Trisomies of most other chromosomes cause such severe disruption that embryos do not survive.
